blocks.text: In line with the 2014 World Health Assembly resolution 67.22 and the 2008 African Union resolution 141 on Access to Essential Medicines, the Government of Tanzania, with great pride and deep commitment to the health and well-being of our people, presents the Revised Standard Treatment Guidelines and the National Essential Medicines List 2026. This edition represents a significant milestone in our ongoing effort to strengthen the delivery of equitable, high-quality, evidence-based health care services across all levels of the healthcare system. This commitment is well enshrined in Article 14 of the 1977 Constitution of the United Republic of Tanzania, which states that everyone has the right to life and to receive protection of their life from society, in accordance with the law. Access to safe, effective, and affordable medicines guided by clear, context-appropriate clinical standards is fundamental to achieving Universal Health Insurance (UHI) and improving health outcomes for all Tanzanians.

blocks.text: Aligned with the 2009 Public Health Act, Tanzania has made notable progress over the years in reducing maternal and child morbidity and mortality, combating communicable and non-communicable diseases, and addressing emerging and re- emerging public health threats. According to the 2007 National Health Policy Paragraph 5.41b(v) and 5.4.3c(i) and Tanzania Vision 2050, the Government of Tanzania, working with its partners, is mandated to provide stewardship in ensuring an affordable, adequate and safe supply of quality medicine and nutrition products to all health facilities and the community in need. In light of the above, and given evolving disease patterns, emerging scientific evidence, antimicrobial resistance, and persistent health system gaps, the regular review of the Standard Treatment Guidelines and National Essential Medicine List (STG/NEMLIT) is important. Periodic updates ensure alignment with the Essential Medicines List, promote the rational use of medicines, enhance the quality and standardisation of care, improve cost-effectiveness, and ensure that treatment recommendations remain responsive to national priorities and the changing health needs of the population.

blocks.text: This 2026 revision has been undertaken through an inclusive, consultative and transparent process engaging stakeholders from the Ministry of Health and its Institutions, the Prime Minister's Office, the Regional Administration and Local Government, Frontline healthcare workers from primary to tertiary health care facilities, both public and private, Professional associations, Academic institutions and implementing partners. Different levels of evidence, from local to regional epidemiological data, pharmacoeconomic analyses, and the 24th World Health Organisation (WHO) Model List of Essential Medicines, have guided the review process and the selection of National Essential Medicines, ensuring relevance to the Tanzanian context, disease burden, and available resources.

blocks.text: The revised Standard Treatment Guidelines provide clear, practical clinical pathways for the diagnosis, treatment and referral of priority conditions encountered in our health facilities. These Guidelines are designed to support health care providers at the primary and tertiary levels of the health care system in making informed clinical decisions that enhance patient outcomes. The accompanying National Essential Medicines List reflects our commitment to rational use of medicines, prioritising those interventions that are scientifically proven, cost-effective and aligned with national health priorities. Further, the document will guide the procurement and supply of medicines at the Medical Stores Department (MSD), the prescribing and dispensing of medicines in public health facilities, and the reimbursement of medicines by the National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF).

blocks.text: We realise that the successful implementation of STG/NEMLIT depends on the collective efforts of all health sector stakeholders. Mentorship, supervision, supply chain management, monitoring and evaluation will be vital to translating STG/NEMLIT into quality of care at the point of service. We call upon all health care professionals and policymakers to champion the adoption and rational use of these tools within their respective spheres of influence.

blocks.text: Finally, we extend our heartfelt appreciation to all individuals and institutions who contributed their expertise, time, insight, and financial support to the development of this seventh edition, 2026. Your dedication has helped shape a resource that will guide clinical practice over the next three years. Together, let us continue to strive for a healthier Tanzania where every person has access to the care they need, when and where they need it.

blocks.text: Lastly, in exercising the powers conferred on me by the President of the United Republic of Tanzania through Government Notice No. 686 19th December of 2025, I hereby declare that the Standard Treatment Guidelines and the National Essential Medicines List – 7th Edition 2026 are endorsed for public use.
